title: Safety Testing for Farm Advisory Chatbots
summary: Test farm advisory chatbots and voice bots in Hindi and regional languages for harmful or wrong advice: invented doses, unregistered products, overconfident diagnoses, scheme errors and data leaks.

seo.title: Safety Testing for Farm Advisory Chatbots | VipraTech
seo.description: Adversarial and accuracy testing of agri advisory chatbots in Hindi and regional languages, with agronomist-confirmed findings and fixes before launch.

problem.intro: Agritech companies and public programmes are putting LLM chatbots and voice bots in front of farmers to answer crop questions. A fluent but wrong answer about a pesticide, a dose or a disease can damage a crop and endanger health, and farmers are likely to trust an answer that sounds confident in their own language.

pain_points.title: Invented or off-label doses
pain_points.detail: LLMs can produce a plausible dose or tank mix that no label supports, or suggest a product not registered for that crop.

pain_points.title: Overconfident diagnosis
pain_points.detail: Bots may name a disease from a vague description or a poor photo instead of asking questions or referring to an agronomist.

pain_points.title: Answers that change by language
pain_points.detail: A bot that behaves carefully in English may give different, less careful answers in Hindi, Marathi or Telugu.

pain_points.title: Manipulation and misinformation
pain_points.detail: Users can push a bot off its rules, and wrong answers on subsidies, schemes or loan terms damage trust in the programme.

solution.overview: We build and run a safety test programme for your farm advisory bot before launch and after every major change. With your agronomists, we define safe behaviour: which topics must be referred, which products and doses are allowed, and how uncertainty should be expressed. We then create multi-turn test conversations in English, Hindi and your regional languages, covering pesticide and dose questions, look-alike symptoms, out-of-season and out-of-region crops, scheme and loan queries, attempts to make the bot ignore its rules, and requests for other farmers' data. Answers are scored automatically against the rules, then agronomists review every risky or failed case. You receive PASS, RISK and FAIL findings with transcripts and specific fixes.
capabilities: Safety policy written with your agronomists: referral topics, allowed products and dose rules
Multi-turn test conversations in English, Hindi and regional languages
Checks for invented doses, unregistered products and unsafe mixing advice
Diagnosis behaviour tests with vague descriptions and poor-quality photos
Rule-bypass, misinformation and data-leakage test sets
PASS, RISK and FAIL findings with transcripts, root causes and fixes

workflow.title: Agree the safety policy
workflow.detail: We work with your agronomists to define referral topics, allowed products, dose rules and how uncertainty must be stated.

workflow.title: Build the test sets
workflow.detail: We create multi-turn conversations and photo cases across crops, regions, languages and risk categories.

workflow.title: Run the tests
workflow.detail: Test conversations run against your bot through its API, a WhatsApp test number or a voice test line.

workflow.title: Score automatically
workflow.detail: Rule checks and an evaluator model score each answer and mark anything risky or failed.

workflow.title: Agronomist review
workflow.detail: Agronomists review every RISK and FAIL case and confirm the finding and its severity.

workflow.title: Report and retest
workflow.detail: You receive findings with fixes, and we rerun the suite after your changes to confirm they hold.

inputs: Access to the bot in a test environment via API, WhatsApp or voice
System prompt, knowledge base and approved advisory content
Approved product and dose list from your agronomists
De-identified past user conversations, where available
outputs: Findings graded PASS, RISK or FAIL with transcripts
Reusable regression suite for future releases
human_in_the_loop: Agronomists confirm every RISK and FAIL finding and set its severity, because only they can judge whether a crop answer is unsafe. Your product team decides which fixes to make and when to release.

Issue tracker such as Jira or Linear
guardrails: Testing only in a test environment or on test numbers, never with real farmers
No real farmer data in test prompts
Findings shared only with named contacts
Severity confirmed by agronomists, not by the evaluator model alone
Regression suite versioned with each bot release
compliance_notes: Test categories map to OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications risks such as prompt injection, sensitive information disclosure and misinformation.
Findings help show that pesticide guidance stays within uses registered under the Insecticides Act 1968, as defined by your agronomists.

Share of findings that pass on retest after your changes.

faqs.q: Do you test in regional languages or only English?
faqs.a: Both. We run the same safety cases in English, Hindi and your regional languages, because bots often behave differently across languages. Native speakers check the test wording.

faqs.q: Who decides whether an answer is unsafe?
faqs.a: Your agronomists, supported by our rule checks and evaluator model. We prepare the cases and evidence; they confirm each finding and its severity.

faqs.q: Can you test a voice bot as well as a chatbot?
faqs.a: Yes. We run spoken test calls against voice bots, including noisy audio and mixed-language speech, and score the transcripts the same way.

faqs.q: Will testing affect our live users?
faqs.a: No. Tests run against a test environment or dedicated test numbers, with no real farmer data in the prompts.
